title: US Faces Largest Cyclosporiasis Outbreak on Record With Over 11,500 Cases Across 41 States
excerpt: The CDC has linked the parasitic outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, with Michigan reporting over 7,000 cases alone. No deaths have been reported.
body:
• The CDC has identified over 11,500 cyclosporiasis cases this season — 4,173 confirmed and about 7,400 under investigation — making it the largest cyclospora outbreak in US history.
  • Michigan is the epicenter with over 7,000 cases; shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico, served at Taco Bell locations, has been identified as the likely source.
  • Taylor Farms has recalled iceberg lettuce shipped to 27 states; the produce went to Walmart, Jack in the Box, and food service operations beyond Taco Bell.
  • No deaths have been reported, but at least 308 people have been hospitalized nationwide, with Michigan alone reporting 102 hospitalizations.

A Parasitic Outbreak of Unprecedented Scale

The United States is grappling with the largest cyclosporiasis outbreak ever recorded, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reporting more than 11,500 cases across 41 states as of late July 2026. Of those, 4,173 cases are laboratory-confirmed, while roughly 7,400 additional cases reported by state and local health departments are undergoing further testing and analysis.

The outbreak dwarfs previous records. According to the US Department of Agriculture, the largest cyclospora outbreak on record previously involved about 1,500 cases linked to contaminated raspberries. By contrast, the CDC has already linked 1,644 confirmed cases to a single multistate cluster centered in the Midwest, with case counts still climbing.

"We do have the outbreak under control."

— Robert F. Kennedy Jr., US Health and Human Services Secretary

Tracing the Source to Shredded Lettuce

Federal and state investigators have traced the large Midwestern outbreak to shredded iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms de Mexico to Taco Bell restaurants in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia. Michigan health officials said they completed more than 2,000 interviews with infected patients, finding "very strong" evidence linking the outbreak to that single product.

Taylor Fresh Foods has since recalled all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico, affecting shipments to 27 states. The contaminated produce also went to Walmart, Jack in the Box, and various food service operations. Taco Bell said it removed Taylor Farms lettuce from its restaurants and its nationwide supply chain.

The FDA initially reported a positive test for cyclospora on Taylor Farms produce at the US-Mexican border, but the result was later deemed a false positive following quality-control checks. The agency said its traceback and epidemiological evidence still points to the company's central Mexico operations. Mexico's Health Minister David Kershenobich said there is no evidence so far that Mexican lettuce caused the outbreak.

Michigan Bears the Brunt

Michigan has been the hardest hit, with state health officials reporting 7,171 cases and 102 hospitalizations. Ohio follows with at least 1,244 cases and 88 hospitalizations, while Indiana has reported 511 cases, West Virginia 195 cases with 15 hospitalizations, and Kentucky 192 cases with 9 hospitalizations.

Despite the scale of the outbreak, no deaths have been reported. The CDC noted that 308 people have been hospitalized nationally among confirmed cases. Doctors say the true number of infections is likely much higher because many cases are never diagnosed or reported.

A Parasite That's Hard to Pin Down

Cyclospora cayetanensis is a microscopic single-cell parasite that only infects humans and cannot be spread through meat. It contaminates produce through exposure to human fecal matter containing the parasite's oocysts, the resistant form that survives outside the body. Symptoms — including explosive watery diarrhea, cramping, nausea, and fatigue — can take up to two weeks to appear, making it difficult for patients to recall what they ate.

The long incubation period compounds the challenge: by the time an outbreak is traced to a supplier, the contaminated product has often already been consumed or discarded, according to Dr. Thomas Lew, an assistant clinical professor at Stanford University School of Medicine. The parasite also cannot be cultured in labs, slowing confirmation compared with most foodborne pathogens.

What Indian Americans Should Know

Fresh produce is a staple in South Asian cooking, and the CDC's guidance applies broadly: avoid shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, particularly at Taco Bell locations in the five affected states. For foods eaten raw, thoroughly wash produce for at least one minute, though washing may not eliminate all cyclospora spores. Cooking to an internal temperature of at least 158°F kills the parasite. Anyone experiencing diarrhea lasting longer than 48 hours should contact a healthcare provider — a short course of the antibiotic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole typically clears the infection.

What's Next

The CDC said the cyclosporiasis season typically runs from May through August, meaning several more weeks of potential exposure remain. Multiple investigations beyond the Midwest cluster are ongoing, and the agency expects more cases to be reported. The epidemiological curve of new infections has not yet slowed, even as Taylor Farms lettuce exits the supply chain. Federal investigators continue working to determine whether other foods or suppliers are involved.
